stem: In migraine prophylaxis, how does topiramate compare with propranolol?

options.text: It is more effective but has a higher risk of behaviour disorders
It is less effective and should only be used in girls of childbearing age
It is primarily used as a calcium channel blocker
It has been proven ineffective in well-controlled trials
It is preferred because it has no significant adverse effects

explanation: Topiramate is more effective for migraine prophylaxis than propranolol, but it has a higher risk of behavioural adverse effects.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because topiramate offers better migraine prevention but is associated with behavioural changes and other neuropsychiatric adverse effects.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because this describes neither the comparative effectiveness nor the main safety concern for topiramate in migraine prophylaxis.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because topiramate is an antiepileptic medicine, not a calcium channel blocker.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because topiramate is effective for migraine prevention, although adverse effects limit its use.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because topiramate can cause clinically important adverse effects, including behavioural changes, so it is not free of significant toxicity.
